headline_marked: [[Bill Gates features Bangladeshi scientist Firdausi Qadri]] in new video on cholera vaccine
headline: Bill Gates features Bangladeshi scientist Firdausi Qadri in new video on cholera vaccine
summary: The video highlights Dr. Qadri's groundbreaking work in developing and implementing affordable oral cholera vaccines, crucial for high-risk areas like Bangladesh.
details: Technology entrepreneur Bill Gates released a video on October 7 across his social media platforms, discussing the oral cholera vaccine. He highlighted the ongoing large-scale vaccination program in Bangladesh, which many have already participated in.

The first dose of the oral cholera vaccine was administered from August 22 to September 26 in 14 high-risk areas across Dhaka, Kishoreganj, Narayanganj, Munshiganj, and Brahmanbaria. The program targets individuals aged one year and above, excluding pregnant women.

To achieve complete protection against cholera, a total of two doses are required. The second dose is currently being administered from September 26 to October 25 through various schools and local health centers.

In his video, Bill Gates emphasized that cholera is a severe diarrheal disease primarily spread through contaminated water, which can be rapidly fatal if untreated. He specifically mentioned Bangladeshi scientist Firdausi Qadri's pivotal work in using this vaccine to halt cholera outbreaks.

The risk of cholera is higher in densely populated countries like Bangladesh, where access to safe drinking water and improved sanitation systems is limited. While long-term prevention requires robust water and sanitation infrastructure, these are often time-consuming and expensive to establish.

This is where the oral cholera vaccine plays a crucial role, offering a quick and effective solution to prevent the disease. It is easy to produce, affordable, and administered orally instead of by injection, making it highly accessible.

Gates further stated that this easily acceptable vaccine can prevent a deadly disease like cholera. He credited Dr. Firdausi Qadri and her co-researchers for saving countless lives through their dedicated work.

Dr. Qadri mentioned Bangladesh's national cholera control plan, which provides clear guidelines on when and where to administer vaccines. Implementing this comprehensive plan and roadmap effectively requires approximately 100 million vaccine doses.

The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation has long supported research and innovation for low-cost oral cholera vaccines in Bangladesh. They have particularly collaborated with icddr,b and Dr. Qadri to make these affordable vaccines widely available. Gates' video is part of this ongoing awareness campaign.

Dr. Firdausi Qadri is an internationally renowned researcher, recognized with the Independence Award (2013) and the Ramon Magsaysay Award (2021). She currently heads the Mucosal Immunology and Vaccinology Unit at icddr,b. This is not the first time Bill Gates has featured her research and contributions.

headline_marked: [[Maha Ashtami and Kumari Puja celebrated across Bangladesh]] today as part of Sharadiya Durga Utsav
headline: Maha Ashtami and Kumari Puja celebrated across Bangladesh today as part of Sharadiya Durga Utsav
summary: Devotees honor womanhood by worshipping young girls as goddesses in Kumari Puja, a special attraction of the Ashtami rituals, believing each woman embodies the power of Mahamaya.
details: Maha Ashtami of Sharadiya Durga Utsav is being celebrated today, Monday, October 19. Religious rituals and worship of Mahamaya are underway at the Ramakrishna Mission in Dhaka.
Kumari Puja is a special attraction of the Ashtami worship. Devotees honor womanhood by worshipping young girls, aged 1 to 16, as goddesses, believing each woman embodies the power of Mahamaya.
Ashtami Puja begins with Chandi recitation, Pushpanjali, and various religious ceremonies. It is believed that on this day, the Goddess defeated the demon Kolasura.

The Maha Ashtami Kalparambha and Bijit Puja commenced at the Ramakrishna Mission in Dhaka before sunrise. The Kumari Devi will be seated on the altar at 9:30 AM, followed by her worship with Panchanaibedya.
caption:
Maha Ashtami of Sharadiya Durga Utsav is being celebrated today across Bangladesh, featuring the special Kumari Puja.

Maha Ashtami of Sharadiya Durga Utsav is being celebrated today, Monday, October 19. Religious rituals and worship of Mahamaya are underway at the Ramakrishna Mission in Dhaka.

Kumari Puja is a special attraction of the Ashtami worship. Devotees honor womanhood by worshipping young girls, aged 1 to 16, as goddesses, believing each woman embodies the power of Mahamaya.

Ashtami Puja begins with Chandi recitation, Pushpanjali, and various religious ceremonies. It is believed that on this day, the Goddess defeated the demon Kolasura.

The Maha Ashtami Kalparambha and Bijit Puja commenced at the Ramakrishna Mission in Dhaka before sunrise. The Kumari Devi will be seated on the altar at 9:30 AM, followed by her worship with Panchanaibedya.
